correctness.rationale: For all positive r,kappa,D,b, the exponential-age OU Gaussian mixture is positive, continuous, normalized and is the unique invariant law by same-reset coupling. On (0,b) the distributional stationary equation implies e^{a x^2}p' derivative=(r-kappa)e^{a x^2}p/D, with p'(0)=0, fixing the derivative sign globally; for x>b each Gaussian component is strictly decreasing and integration preserves this sign. At r=kappa the explicit critical plateau and decaying Gaussian-tail primitive meet continuously at b and satisfy the exact -r/(2D) slope jump, normalization, and positivity. The plateau-mass integral is pointwise strictly increasing in dimensionless separation and dominated convergence yields both endpoints. The standalone Python 3 standard-library quadrature checker passed 291 finite assertions across 15 parameter cases; these finite diagnostics do not replace analytical proof.

value.rationale: The number and locations of stationary modes govern qualitative concentration of nonequilibrium trapped particles under distributed resets. A universal exactly flat critical distribution for all positive source separations and diffusivities, together with a sharp one-mode/plateau/two-mode classification and exact critical plateau mass, is a structural global shape result rather than a mere substitution into a moment formula or a small numerical increment. The result precisely isolates competition between resetting and harmonic relaxation and can guide experimental reset scheduling and distribution design; it makes no unsupported claim of a general nonlinear-trap theorem.
